works_well.theme: One post reaches everyone, so far fewer calls and texts
works_well.what_it_means: Caregivers write one update and the whole circle of family and friends sees it, instead of answering each person.

quotes.quote: I was responding to 50-60 texts a day with everyone saying "Keep me posted" or "Let me know what they are saying".
I had literally 100+ people wanting updates on her condition. This app allowed me to accomplish the task with a single daily post.

works_well.theme: Frees the caregiver's time to be with the sick person
works_well.what_it_means: Less time spent updating people means more time and energy for the patient and for the caregiver's own tasks.

quotes.quote: And you can spend your time as a caregiver where it needs to be; with the patient!
It frees me up to do more for my wife

works_well.theme: Easy to use for posting and reading
works_well.what_it_means: Writers and readers describe the app as simple, quick to post in, and easy to read.

quotes.quote: Very user friendly for both author and readers.
Posting journal entries is super easy though.

works_well.theme: Family far away can follow along and feel close
works_well.what_it_means: Relatives in other states or countries, or who cannot visit, keep up with the patient through the posts.

quotes.quote: Even family members in Europe can keep up to date.
My 85 year young mama can catch up from her phone and see the pictures- very helpful to visit without the long travel.

works_well.theme: Comments and messages lift up the family
works_well.what_it_means: Readers send love, prayers and encouragement back, which supports the patient and the caregiver.

quotes.quote: My son's spirits were boosted by all of the feedback and encouragement he received.
The outpouring of support our family receives in return lightens our load and lifts our spirits.

works_well.theme: Same site works again for each new health crisis
works_well.what_it_means: Families come back to the same tool, or the same page, across years and repeat illnesses.

quotes.quote: I was very pleased that her site was still in place and working after two plus years.
After not using it for 3 years she had a relapse I was able to restart it with no problems

works_well.theme: Everyone gets the same accurate news at the same time
works_well.what_it_means: One shared source cuts down on mixed messages and rumors between relatives.

quotes.quote: Caring Bridge assures that everyone gets the same information at the same time.
It is an amazing resource to update in real time and eliminate miscommunication.

works_well.theme: Only invited people can see the updates
works_well.what_it_means: Families like that the page stays inside a chosen group instead of public social media.

quotes.quote: Keeps the tender and raw moments within a chosen group instead of the whole internet gawking.
You can limit viewing to only those you grant permission.

works_well.theme: Doubles as a journal and record of what happened
works_well.what_it_means: Posts build a dated history of the illness that families value keeping.

quotes.quote: It also provides a way to record what happens and when.
My niece posted every day, so it also became her medical journal.

works_well.theme: Readers get alerts and choose how closely to follow
works_well.what_it_means: Followers can sign up for notices of new posts or just check in when they want.

quotes.quote: People can sign up to get notifications or just check the app for new posts.
They can choose for themselves whether or not to receive all of the updates

works_well.theme: Reaches relatives who are not on Facebook
works_well.what_it_means: It gets news to people who do not use social media, or links with Facebook to reach more people.

quotes.quote: especially for folks not on Facebook
simple integration with Facebook, which enabled me to reach even more people.

does_not_work_well.theme: Posting from the app freezes, loses posts, or mangles photos
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Writers report autosave hangs, posts not submitting, drafts and photos lost, or photos turned sideways.

quotes.quote: Once I am done writing, it gets stuck on autosave and I can’t post.
photos disappear from drafts, submitting a post doesn't always actually submit the post

does_not_work_well.theme: App is weaker than the website, so people switch
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Several reviewers say the website works well but the phone app does not, and fall back to a computer.

quotes.quote: I really like caring bridge when I access it on my computer- it's a phenomenal way to keep family/friends updated. But this phone app leaves so much to be desired.
Am deleting the app and going straight to the webpage.

does_not_work_well.theme: After the 2024 update, features broke or went missing
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: The redesigned app lost photos and drafts, showed wrong dates and counts, broke shared links and dropped text alerts.

quotes.quote: Most of my photos, including profile pics, have disappeared.
please bring back text notifications when there is a new post. We are missing many crucial updates for a sick family member.

does_not_work_well.theme: Hard to find your way around the app
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Settings and past journal entries are hard to reach, and the layout feels dated.

quotes.quote: Why can't I see all the journal entries in one list?
Navigating the site settings is unintuitive.

does_not_work_well.theme: After the 2024 update, family could not sign in
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: A sign-in change in mid-2024 locked out authors and readers, especially older relatives.

quotes.quote: So many of my over 60 relatives have been not able to reaccess their account.
As the caregivers we should not be your I.T. Department.

does_not_work_well.theme: Not built for day-to-day care coordination
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: People caring with siblings, or arranging meals, find it is a news feed, not a tool for daily tasks.

quotes.quote: they seem better for sharing health updates with extended family than for the day-to-day coordination between us.
I do wish the meal train was included on this site rather than a third-party site.

does_not_work_well.what_it_means: The donate banner keeps asking even after giving, and some readers think gifts go to the family.

quotes.quote: it continues to state that we need to donate to caring bridge again, and that no one from her page has donated.
The only thing with the app that I don't love is the donate button being front and center.

does_not_work_well.theme: Can't easily see who read or reacted
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Authors want to see who visited and who left hearts, and the app hides or miscounts this.

quotes.quote: it always shows 0 comments and 0 reactions when there actually are reactions and comments
You cannot see who hearts a post from the app.

who_uses_and_who_pays.theme: A spouse or parent usually posts; relatives and friends read
who_uses_and_who_pays.what_it_means: The writer is most often the patient's husband, wife or parent, with grandparents, cousins and friends following.

quotes.quote: Updating everyone at same time allowed me to focus on my husband and his recovery.
This is so much easier for my daughter and son-in-law to send updates to friends and family in one message.

who_uses_and_who_pays.theme: Free to use; families donate to keep it going
who_uses_and_who_pays.what_it_means: No one reports paying a fee; several say they gave money by choice.

quotes.quote: The website is free to use and donations do not go to the families.
our family and friends have donated thousands of dollars to this app to keep it going.

relatives_joining_and_sharing.theme: Share one link and people follow, often without signing up
relatives_joining_and_sharing.what_it_means: Families send one link or invite and readers join on their own terms.

quotes.quote: I just sent one email with the Caring Bridge link to everyone who might be interested in following his progress.
visitors can get information without having to sign up.

relatives_joining_and_sharing.theme: Older relatives got locked out when sign-in changed
relatives_joining_and_sharing.what_it_means: When accounts became required or changed, older readers could not get back in.

quotes.quote: Now since the update barely anyone can even sign in.
Your dealing with old people and technology changes are hard on them.

relatives_joining_and_sharing.theme: More than one family member can post
relatives_joining_and_sharing.what_it_means: Co-authors share the job of writing updates.

quotes.quote: There are two of us posting to the site so we can avoid sending duplicate updates.
I'm a co-author on a site for my dad while he battles pancreatic cancer

cost_price_cancelling.theme: Free, but donation prompts are pushy
cost_price_cancelling.what_it_means: The service costs nothing, yet donation banners and buttons bother some families.

quotes.quote: your developers should really trigger the funding banner to sleep after a donation has been made
The website is free to use and donations do not go to the families.

setup_and_ease_of_use.theme: Easy to start and easy to restart
setup_and_ease_of_use.what_it_means: Setup is described as simple, and old pages come back to life for a new crisis.

quotes.quote: It's easy to manage and use, limiting access to those we approve
it has already streamlined my communications with tons of family and friends while my parents are both in the hospital.

setup_and_ease_of_use.theme: App posting is buggy, so the website is the fallback
setup_and_ease_of_use.what_it_means: The phone app freezes or loses posts, and caregivers copy text over to the website.

quotes.quote: If I am interrupted, which can happen frequently for a caregiver, the issue reoccurs.
I am unable to add any photos or write a journal without issues with the cursor moving downward on the page on its own.

privacy_data_trust.theme: Families trust it as a private, invite-only space
privacy_data_trust.what_it_means: Reviewers value that only approved people see health news.

quotes.quote: it makes a very difficult time easier by allowing me one, secure platform to communicate to loved ones.
being able to share info without compromising health

privacy_data_trust.theme: Lost photos and wrong dates hurt trust in the record
privacy_data_trust.what_it_means: When the update changed dates and removed photos, families worried about their history.

quotes.quote: Having the correct dates is critical!
I can’t believe that user testing would’ve proven the update was ready.

why_people_stop_or_stay.theme: People stay because it saves time in every crisis
why_people_stop_or_stay.what_it_means: Families return to it for each new illness and recommend it to others.

quotes.quote: Caring Bridge is our Go-To app when we have a medical situation.
This is my third experience with Caring Bridge.

why_people_stop_or_stay.theme: People drop the app (not the service) when posting fails
why_people_stop_or_stay.what_it_means: Frustrated writers delete or reinstall the app and keep using the website.

quotes.quote: Huge waste of time.
I've already uninstalled/re-installed the app without any positive results.

what_people_use_instead_or_alongside.theme: Linked with GoFundMe, meal trains, and Facebook
what_people_use_instead_or_alongside.what_it_means: Families pair it with fundraising, meal sign-up and social media tools, which live outside it.

quotes.quote: options for linking in meal train and go fund me links
I cannot connect to GoFundMe through it either.

what_people_use_instead_or_alongside.theme: Group texts, notes and spreadsheets for daily coordination
what_people_use_instead_or_alongside.what_it_means: Siblings sharing care still run day-to-day tasks through group chats and shared notes.

quotes.quote: We've tried group texts but important information gets buried.
a family group chat that never stops

single_mentions.point: A cousin in Australia could not get access; writer asks if it is US only.
Five siblings and twelve grandchildren use it to coordinate being there for a mother with dementia who lives alone.
Share button shows no options on iPad.
Tapping external links crashes the app.
Caregiver used the page to post rules about texting, saying no new post means no change.
Has a calendar so helpers can sign up to support the family.
Caregiver asks followers to support her too, not only the patient.

reader_notes: Most kept items are short Google Play reviews from 2020-2023 that praise the same thing (one update for everyone); many are 5-star and very brief. Problem reviews cluster around the mid-2024 app redesign (sign-in, lost photos, drafts). 15 gp- items were exact copies of g- items and were dropped as duplicates (extra drop reason added). Items marked prefiltered_caregiving were treated as caregiving unless the writer was clearly the patient writing about their own illness (7 dropped). Several kept generic reviews (e.g. 'keep family updated about a loved one') do not name the writer's relationship. Only 6 kept items come from Reddit; no forum item was kept (writers' own caregiving not stated, or no experience). reddit-p1wrnjau is written by someone thinking about building a tool; kept because it gives their own family's experience. No item says anything about customer support response.
